title_as_printed: Can we detect cognitive "super-agers" in Parkinson's disease? Cognitive, neuropsychiatric and motor outcomes in the first 10 years of Parkinson's disease
blind_first: blind codes were written to this file before the registry codes file was opened

Task_Type.reason: Longitudinal multilevel models compare trajectories of three baseline cognitive subgroups (superagers, cognitively normal, PD-MCI) in global cognition, depression, anxiety and motor severity. No classifier, cut-point or discrimination figure. Subtype/group-comparison study, T4 (T6 as a descriptive cohort study would also be arguable).

Category.reason: PPMI cohort data: neuropsychological tests, MoCA, GDS, STAI-T, MDS-UPDRS III. Baseline CSF markers (alpha-synuclein, tau/amyloid ratios) enter only a sensitivity analysis, so C3 is at most a marginal secondary domain.

Validation_Type.reason: No predictive model is fitted or validated: there is no train/test split, held-out partition or cross-validation anywhere in the paper. The analyses are multilevel group-difference models (plus ANOVA of baseline CSF markers). Under the convention a non-model study is V2; V3 (k-fold + held-out test) has no basis.
Validation_Type.quote: Multilevel modeling examined differences between the three cognitive groups (superagers, PD-MCI, cognitively normal) and dependent variables. A separate multilevel modeling analysis was performed for each dependent variable.

Sample_N_Approx.reason: Final analysed sample 689 (from 1135 queried): 233 superagers + 339 cognitively normal + 117 PD-MCI (pp. 3, 5).

ADNI_Dependent.reason: Data from the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI); ADNI not used.

notes: The V3 code places a non-model cohort study in the held-out-test validation tier. Since is_model_study is false, this row should not enter the review's validation-tier statistics at all; if it currently does, it inflates the V3 count.
